title: De Ja Vu Opens at Southampton Royal Pier, Reviving Indian Dining at a Historic Waterfront Venue
excerpt: The contemporary Indian restaurant replaces the former Kuti's Brasserie at the Grade II listed pier where Queen Victoria's own love of curry helped shape British dining history.
body:
• De Ja Vu, a contemporary Indian restaurant, has opened at Southampton's Grade II listed Royal Pier — a waterfront venue with deep ties to Indian culinary history dating back to Queen Victoria's era.
  • New owner Imran Talukder transformed the former Kuti's Brasserie, which had operated at the location for years before closing, with a grand reopening featuring fireworks and a lavish buffet.
  • The restaurant continues a tradition of Indian dining at the Royal Pier that connects back to Queen Victoria, who was introduced to Indian cuisine by her Munshi, Abdul Karim, and reportedly ate curry every day.
  • Southampton's Indian restaurant scene remains vibrant, with establishments like Coriander Lounge and The Chennai Lounge gaining national recognition.

Southampton's historic Royal Pier has a new tenant — and a familiar culinary identity. De Ja Vu, a contemporary Indian restaurant, has opened in the Grade II listed waterfront building that previously housed Kuti's Brasserie, one of the port city's most prominent Indian dining establishments. The grand reopening was marked by a fireworks display over Southampton Water, live DJ entertainment, and a complimentary Indian buffet for invited guests.

A Venue Steeped in Curry History

The Royal Pier is no ordinary restaurant location. Opened by Queen Victoria in 1833, the pier holds a unique connection to the history of Indian cuisine in Britain. After being introduced to Indian food by her Munshi (personal teacher) Abdul Karim on the Isle of Wight, Victoria became a devoted enthusiast — reportedly eating curry every day. That a fine-dining Indian restaurant now occupies the pier's former gate house feels like history completing a circle.

The imposing two-story property offers considerable dining space: 110 covers on the ground floor, 60 on the first floor, a 30-seat Chandelier Cocktail Bar upstairs, and 60 additional seats on a rooftop terrace with panoramic views across Southampton Water. The venue had previously served as Royal Thai before becoming Kuti's Brasserie, then Kuti's of Southampton.

New Ownership, Family Roots

De Ja Vu is led by Imran Talukder, whose connection to the venue runs deeper than a business transaction. The restaurant's name pays homage to the 1980s, when Talukder's father was involved in Southampton's restaurant scene. Previous owner Kuti Miah, the veteran restaurateur who had operated several Indian dining establishments across Hampshire — including Kuti's Express, Kuti's Noorani in Eastleigh, and Kuti's of Wickham near Portsmouth — is not involved in the new venture.

"De Ja Vu marks a new journey for the venue."

— Southampton Times

Contemporary Indian Cuisine in a Historic Setting

The restaurant specializes in authentic Indian flavors presented through a modern lens. Operating seven days a week from 5 PM to 11 PM, De Ja Vu positions itself for both intimate dinners and larger celebrations. The launch party's extensive buffet showcased signature dishes, offering guests a preview of the kitchen's range.

The transformation preserves the venue's architectural heritage while reimagining its interior. Talukder's team has focused on creating an elegant setting that balances the building's Grade II listed character with contemporary dining expectations — a challenge that has defeated previous tenants at heritage properties across the UK.

Southampton's Thriving Indian Food Scene

De Ja Vu enters a competitive but growing market. Southampton has established itself as a genuine hub for Indian cuisine in southern England. Coriander Lounge, located on the city's High Street, has built a reputation for fine-dining Indian food at accessible prices, earning a 4.6-star rating. The Chennai Lounge was named among the UK's top 100 curry restaurants by the Asian Catering Federation in its latest annual guide — a list selected through public votes and expert recommendations.

Other notable Southampton establishments include Bayleaf Kitchen, which features a chef trained in five-star Indian hotels, and Everest Cuisine, which blends Nepali and Indian dishes including traditional momos and thalis alongside tandoori classics.

The Bigger Picture for British Indian Dining

The opening reflects a broader trend in British Indian restaurants: a move toward premium settings, heritage venues, and elevated presentation without abandoning the comfort-food roots that made curry Britain's adopted national dish. The Asian Catering Federation noted that despite rising costs and economic pressures, the sector continues to innovate and attract loyal customers.

For Southampton's Indian diaspora community and curry enthusiasts alike, De Ja Vu represents another option in a city that has quietly built one of the south coast's strongest Indian dining scenes. Whether the Royal Pier's latest chapter can match the longevity of its predecessors remains to be seen, but the venue's history suggests that Indian cuisine and this particular stretch of Southampton waterfront have a connection worth sustaining.
